# Fractional AI Governance Advisor: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Engagement:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Term:** 12 months, renewable, at US$10,000 per month

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this engagement would be its first with the Academy.

The Client's AI portfolio spans three stages:

* A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal.
* AI visual inspection is in pilot on the German production line.
* AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is to start next year, but the start date is not fixed. The incumbent frameworks are ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001, alongside an internal audit function.

The stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints apply:

* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the piloting stage, governance decisions recur rather than arrive once. The Client has one system already in use, one moving toward production and one in planning. Each needs authorization, ownership and evidence at a different point in the year. A single assessment would capture the position on one date and then age. A fractional advisor stays alongside the governance team as each system moves forward.

The program works from three principles:

* **Slow AI:** AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
* **Informed Intent:** no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human:** every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

The working frameworks are:

* the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Executive and board reporting draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement start date is Unknown. Quarters are therefore numbered from the start of the engagement. The sequence puts visual inspection governance first so that it can be completed before the stated Q2 2027 production objective. How the quarters align with Q2 2027 depends on the start date and is confirmed at intake. ISO/IEC 42001 preparation increases in the later quarters. Its external timing is Unknown and is flagged for intake.

**Quarter 1: Establish.** The program will:

* build the AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 internal audit finding;
* draft Informed Intent authorizations for the deployed chatbot and the visual inspection pilot;
* map named owners under Final Liability rests with the Human; and
* set up the monthly cadence.

Visual inspection governance work also begins in this quarter. Two questions go to intake:

* whether works council consultation applies to visual inspection; and
* whether the chatbot processes customer data, and if so where.

**Quarter 2: Gate to Production.** The program will:

* apply the Slow AI tests to visual inspection as a precondition for production;
* complete its authorization, boundaries and exit criteria;
* define human oversight and intervention points; and
* assemble the evidence the executive team will consider before go-live.

Questions about EU AI Act classification and obligations are flagged for verification by external counsel.

**Quarter 3: Assure.** The program will:

* run an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap assessment;
* identify where requirements may connect with the existing ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 frameworks, subject to intake confirmation of what those frameworks currently cover;
* support an internal audit walkthrough of the AI management approach; and
* mature the evidence collection.

The outputs describe readiness, not certification outcomes.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.** The program will:

* prepare authorization and ownership for planned AI sales forecasting before that work begins;
* review how the governance artifacts are performing after visual inspection reaches production;
* refresh ISO/IEC 42001 readiness status; and
* prepare the renewal options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement includes four standing elements:

| Element | Frequency | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Executive advisory session | Monthly | Decisions, risks and direction for the executive team |
| Working session with the governance team | Monthly | Hands-on progress on artifacts and evidence |
| Asynchronous availability | Ongoing, for defined question categories | Questions between sessions |
| Governance review | Quarterly | Progress against the annual arc |

Asynchronous questions cover four categories:

* governance interpretation
* artifact review
* audit preparation
* decision framing

Response windows are agreed at intake. Participants in each session will be confirmed at intake from among these roles: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. How the advisor's working arrangements will respect the requirement that customer data stays in the EU is also confirmed at intake.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**

* governance evolution
* implementation guidance
* audit preparation
* AI strategy
* executive decision support

**Out of scope:**

* legal advice
* certification body functions
* staff augmentation
* incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation and any US regulatory exposure, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised by the advisor are flagged for counsel verification and are not settled advice.

## 6. Price

The fee is US$10,000 per month for 12 months, renewable.

The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The fiscal year dates are Unknown, so it is not yet clear how program months fall across fiscal years. This is a question to confirm at intake before contracting.
